q: 1. Usefullness of plane table is enhanced by providing
explain: The Indian tangent clinometer, when fitted to the alidade, allows vertical angles and elevations to be measured directly during plane tabling, enhancing its usefulness.

q: 2. For the revision of an existing survey with the help of plane table we generally use
explain: Resection allows the plane table position to be located and oriented using already known points on an existing map, making it ideal for revising existing surveys.

q: 3. A point determined by resection on a plane table is called
explain: When the position of the plane table station is determined by resection from known points, the resulting located point is termed a 'plane table fix'.

q: 4. The instrument which is used in plane tabling for obtaining horizontal and vertical distance directly without resorting to chaining, is known as
explain: A telescope alidade, fitted with stadia hairs, allows both horizontal and vertical distances to be measured tacheometrically directly during plane tabling, without chaining.

q: 5. The operation of revolving a plane table about its vertical axis so that all lines on the sheet become parallel to corresponding lines on the ground, is known
explain: Orientation is the process of rotating the plane table so that all lines on the plotted sheet remain parallel to their corresponding lines on the ground.

q: 6. In setting up a plane table at any station
options: both leveling and centering are done simultaneously
explain: When setting up a plane table, leveling and centering are carried out together (simultaneously) as adjustments to one affect the other.

q: 7. While surveying a plot of land by Plane tabling, the field observations
options: and plotting do not proceed simultaneously
and recorded in field books to be plotted later
explain: The key characteristic of plane table surveying is that field observation and plotting are done together at the same time in the field, unlike other methods where plotting is done later in the office.

q: 8. The instrument which is used in plane tabling for obtaining horizontal and vertical distances directly without resorting to chaining, is known as
explain: A telescopic alidade fitted with stadia hairs allows horizontal and vertical distances to be read directly (by tacheometric principles) without chaining, unlike a plain alidade which is only a sighting/ruling device.

q: 9. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by
explain: Inaccessible points (points that cannot be reached to measure distance) are plotted by the method of intersection, sighting the point from two known plane table stations and drawing rays to fix its position.

q: 10. Locating the position of a plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as
explain: The three-point problem is the specific technique of orienting a plane table and fixing the instrument's own station by resection with reference to three known, plotted points.

q: 11. To orient a plane table at a point with two inaccessible points, the method generally adopted is
explain: The two-point problem is the special resection technique used to orient a plane table when only two well-defined but inaccessible points are available for reference.

q: 12. Pick up the method of surveying in which field observations and plotting proceed simultaneously from the following
explain: Plane table surveying is unique in that field observation and plotting are carried out together at the same time in the field.

q: 13. Which one of the following procedures for getting accurate orientation is the most distinctive feature of the art of plane tabling
explain: Resection (particularly the two-point and three-point problems) is considered the most distinctive and skill-demanding feature of plane table surveying, used to orient the table accurately.

q: 14. To instrument resembling an alidade is
explain: The tangent clinometer, mounted with a straight edge for sighting and drawing, closely resembles the working principle and construction of an alidade used in plane tabling.

q: 15. The angle of intersection of the horizon glass and index glass in an optical square is
explain: In an optical square, the two mirrors (horizon glass and index glass) are fixed at 45 degrees to each other, causing the incident ray to be deflected through 90 degrees via double reflection.

q: 16. Methods adopted for traversing are
options: chain traversing and loose needle method
chain angle method and fast needle method
explain: Traversing can be done using various methods such as 'loose needle' (compass), 'fast needle' (theodolite), or by measuring angles between lines using a chain.

q: 17. The technique of plotting all the accessible stations with a single set up of plane table is called
explain: Radiation is the method in which rays are drawn from a single plane table station to each visible (accessible) point, and distances are plotted to scale along these rays, all from one setup.

q: 18. Radiation plane table survey is the best suited when
explain: Radiation requires measuring the actual distance from the instrument station to each point, so it is best suited when the points are both close by and physically accessible for chaining.

q: 19. An advantage of plane tabling is
options: chances to miss details are less.
explain: Because plotting is done in the field itself while the ground is in view, there is little chance of any topographic detail being missed, which is a key advantage of plane table surveying.

q: 20. Plotting of inaccessible points on a plane table, is done by
explain: Points that are inaccessible (cannot be reached to measure distance) but are visible from two known plane table stations are plotted using the intersection method.

q: 21. Locating the position of plane table station with reference to three known points, is known as
explain: When the plane table station's position is determined with reference to three known points visible on the ground, this is specifically termed the three-point problem (a case of resection).

q: 22. The 'fix' of a plane table from three known points, is good, if
options: either the right or left station is nearest
explain: As per the book's answer key, the quality of the 'fix' from three-point resection depends on the geometric configuration (strength of fix relative to the great circle), not simply on which station is nearest, so none of these applies directly.

q: 23. The process of putting the plane table into some fixed position so that a line representing certain direction of the plane is parallel to the direction in the field is known as
explain: Orientation is the process of aligning the plane table so that lines drawn on the sheet are parallel to the corresponding lines/directions on the ground.

q: 24. Which one of the following is known as instrumental error in plane table surveying?
explain: Non-horizontality of the plane table board is an instrumental (equipment set-up) error, as distinct from personal errors like defective sighting, orientation, or centering.

q: 25. Accurate centering of a plane table is done by
explain: A plumbing fork (with a plumb bob) is the instrument used to accurately centre the plane table exactly over the ground station point.

q: 26. The working edge of an alidade, is known as
explain: The straight ruling edge of an alidade against which sighting/drawing lines are drawn is specifically called the fiducial edge.

q: 27. In the method of plane table survey the object to be plotted is sighted from two plane table stations. This method is called as
explain: Sighting the same object from two different, known plane table stations and plotting its position at the intersection of the two resulting rays is the method of intersection.

q: 28. Finding the location of the station occupied by the table, on the sheet by means of sighting to three well defined points whose locations have been previously plotted on the sheet, is known as
explain: This specific technique of locating the occupied plane table station using three known, already-plotted points is called the three-point problem.

q: 29. The traversing by the method of deflection angles is chiefly used in
explain: The deflection angle method of traversing is commonly used across all types of linear engineering works - canals, highways, and railways - since it directly gives the angle by which the alignment changes at each station.

q: 30. The distances AC and BC are measured from two fixed points A and B whose distance AB is known. The point C is plotted by intersection. This method is generally adopted in
explain: Locating an unknown point C by measuring/computing angles or distances from two known points A and B on a fixed baseline, and plotting by intersection, is the basic principle of triangulation.

q: 31. The size of plane table is
explain: A standard plane table board used in surveying is typically 750 mm x 900 mm in size.

q: 32. The two point problem and three point problem are methods of
explain: Both the two-point problem and three-point problem are specific techniques used to solve the resection problem in plane table surveying - determining the plane table's own position from known points.

q: 33. The method of surveying in which field work and plotting work are done simultaneously, is called
explain: As established, plane table surveying is the unique method where field observation and plotting proceed together, simultaneously.

q: 34. In plane tabling, the instrument used to measure horizontal and vertical distances directly, is known as
explain: As noted earlier, a telescopic alidade, fitted with stadia hairs, allows both horizontal and vertical distances to be measured directly in plane table surveying.

q: 35. The plane table surveying is
options: most suitable for preparing small-scale maps
less costly than a theodolite survey
explain: Plane table surveying is well suited for small-scale mapping, is unaffected by local magnetic attraction (unlike compass surveys), and is generally less costly than theodolite surveying, so all the listed statements are true.

q: 36. The operation of turning the table so that all the lines on the paper are parallel to the corresponding lines on the ground, is called
explain: As defined earlier, this act of aligning the plane table so that plotted lines are parallel to the corresponding ground lines is called orientation.

q: 37. The plotting of small areas which can be commanded from a single station, is usually done on the plane table by the method of
explain: When a small area can be entirely observed and measured from one single station, the method of radiation is used to plot all the points directly from that station.

q: 38. The method of intersection in plane tabling is commonly used for
options: locating the distant and inaccessible points
locating the points which may be used subsequently as the instrument stations
explain: Intersection is a versatile method used to locate distant/inaccessible points, broken boundary details, and even future instrument stations, so all the listed uses apply.

q: 39. The method of plane tabling commonly used for establishing the instrument stations only, is a
explain: Resection is specifically used to locate/establish the plane table's own instrument station with reference to already plotted points.

q: 40. Spirit level in plane table is used for
explain: The spirit level fitted to (or used with) a plane table is specifically used to check and set the table perfectly horizontal, i.e., for levelling the table.

q: 41. Intersection is preferred to radiation when
options: it is not possible to measure any distance
the points are too far and invisible
explain: Intersection is preferred over radiation specifically when the points to be located are inaccessible, so their distance cannot be directly measured, requiring rays from two known stations instead.

q: 42. The strength of fix is poor when
options: the station is within the great triangle
the station is outside the great circle
the station is within the great circle but outside the great triangle
the station is on the great circle
explain: In the three-point resection problem, the strength of fix is poor when the plane table station lies within the great circle (through the three known points) but outside the great triangle formed by them.

q: 43. An advantage of plane tabling is
options: changes to miss details are less
explain: A key advantage of plane tabling is that plotting is done outdoors in the field itself, alongside the observations, reducing the chance of errors from later office plotting.

q: 44. The types of survey in which field work and plotting proceeds simultaneously
explain: Plane table surveying is unique because the map is drawn in the field while the observations are being made.

q: 45. Plane table surveying is graphical method of surveying in which
options: field work and plotting proceeds simultaneously
plotting is done later while records are taken in field book
explain: The primary advantage of plane table surveying is that the map is prepared in the field directly, eliminating the need for a separate field book.

q: 46. Setting up the plane table consists of operations
explain: Basic setup involves getting the board horizontal (levelling) and placing the plotted point exactly over the ground station (centering).

q: 47. Plane table survey is considered good as compared to other survey since
options: chances to missing details are less
explain: Since plotting happens while looking at the actual terrain, the surveyor is much less likely to omit important features.

q: 48. A disadvantage of plane table survey is
options: It is heavy, cumbersome and awkward to carry
It can't be used in wet climate
details may not be available while redrawing to a different scale
accessories are likely to be lost
explain: The large board and tripod make it physically more difficult to transport compared to a compass or a simple level.

q: 49. Placing the table over the station such that the station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on the ground is
explain: Centering ensures the vertical axis of the plotted point and the ground station are aligned.

q: 50. Orientation is the operation of keeping the table at successive stations such that
options: the position of the table at the station is parallel to the position it occupied at the previous station
the position of station plotted on sheet is exactly above the corresponding station on ground
the table is brought in a horizontal plane
explain: Orientation ensures that every line on the paper remains parallel to its corresponding line on the ground.
